reference: Values are gameplay-tuned from public mission datasheets. Dimensions in metres. Mass in kg. Cost in USD.

parts.name: Rutherford Cluster (3x)
parts.description: Three small electric-pump-fed kerolox engines. Light, restartable, and the bottom end of the orbital launch market.
parts.heritage: Based on Rocket Lab Electron first stage.

parts.name: Light Thrust Structure
parts.description: A composite truss for small launch vehicles. Carries the engine load into the tank walls.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and LauncherOne thrust structures.

parts.name: RP-1 Tank (Small)
parts.description: A small kerosene tank for lightweight vehicles. Same fuel as the big rockets, half the mass.
parts.heritage: Based on small launch vehicle tankage.

parts.name: LOX Tank (Small)
parts.description: A small liquid oxygen tank. Same cryogenic handling as the larger LOX tanks, less propellant.
parts.heritage: Based on small launch vehicle tankage.

parts.name: Light Intertank
parts.description: A small intertank structure for lightweight two-stage vehicles.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and Firefly Alpha intertanks.

parts.name: Small Interstage
parts.description: A lightweight interstage for small two-stage vehicles. Jettisoned at separation.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and Rocket 3 interstages.

parts.name: Standard Nose Cone
parts.description: A simple ogive shape that covers the payload during ascent. Jettisoned once above the atmosphere.
parts.heritage: Flown on nearly every atmospheric launch vehicle since the 1950s.

parts.name: Reinforced Nose Cone
parts.description: Thicker skin and a heat-resistant cap for launches that pass through denser atmosphere or higher dynamic pressure.
parts.heritage: Common on vehicles flying heavy payloads through max-Q.

parts.name: Sensor Nose Cone
parts.description: Carries a small instrument package behind a transparent window in the tip. Adds a camera or probe ahead of the main payload.
parts.heritage: Flown on atmospheric probe missions and upper stage test flights.

parts.name: Apollo-Class Guidance Unit
parts.description: A flight computer, inertial measurement unit, and star tracker in a single box. The entry-level option for steering and navigation.
parts.heritage: Heritage design pattern from Apollo and Shuttle-era flight computers.

parts.name: Rad-Hard Flight Computer
parts.description: Hardened against ionising radiation. Required for missions to Jupiter's belts or long-duration inner solar system flights.
parts.heritage: Flown on Juno, Europa Clipper, and every mission past the asteroid belt.

parts.name: Autonomy Package
parts.description: Onboard software and additional processors that let the spacecraft handle known faults without waiting for commands from Earth.
parts.heritage: Based on Deep Space 1's Remote Agent and later autonomy research.

parts.name: Camera Suite
parts.description: A multi-spectral imaging system. Low mass, low power, and the workhorse instrument on most flyby missions.
parts.heritage: Based on Mastcam-Z (Perseverance) and LORRI (New Horizons).

parts.name: Mass Spectrometer
parts.description: Analyses the chemical composition of gases and surface material. Detects organic molecules at parts-per-billion sensitivity.
parts.heritage: SAM (Curiosity), MOMA (ExoMars).

parts.name: Drill and Sample Cache
parts.description: Rotary percussive drill with a sealed sample container. Required for any mission that returns material to Earth.
parts.heritage: Based on Curiosity and Perseverance sampling systems.

parts.name: Ground-Penetrating Radar
parts.description: Maps subsurface ice and rock layers from orbit or a flyby. The primary tool for studying icy moons.
parts.heritage: MARSIS (Mars Express), REASON (Europa Clipper).

parts.name: Magnetometer Boom
parts.description: A long boom that holds a magnetic field sensor away from the spacecraft's own electronics. Cheap and scientifically useful.
parts.heritage: Flown on Voyager, Galileo, Juno, and most outer planet missions.

parts.name: Solar Array (Small)
parts.description: A single deployable solar panel. Output scales with distance from the Sun, so it is only practical inside the asteroid belt.
parts.heritage: Standard on inner solar system satellites.

parts.name: Solar Array (Large)
parts.description: A pair of large deployable wings with higher output. Same distance limitation as the small array but four times the power.
parts.heritage: Based on Juno's three-wing configuration and Psyche's solar arrays.

parts.name: RTG (Pu-238)
parts.description: Radioisotope thermoelectric generator. Converts heat from plutonium decay into electricity. Works anywhere, but the supply of Pu-238 is limited.
parts.heritage: Voyager, Cassini, New Horizons, Curiosity, Perseverance.

parts.name: Battery Pack
parts.description: Stores energy for eclipse periods and high-power manoeuvres. Required with solar arrays because panels produce nothing at night.
parts.heritage: Li-ion chemistry based on Mars rover and ISS batteries.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (Small)
parts.description: High-efficiency propellant tank for the upper stage. Light and compact.
parts.heritage: Based on Centaur and Falcon 9 second stage tank designs.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (Large)
parts.description: A larger upper stage tank for missions that need more delta-V after stage separation.
parts.heritage: Based on Centaur III and Ariane 5 ESC-A upper stages.

parts.name: Vacuum Engine (Small)
parts.description: A vacuum-optimised engine with a large nozzle for high specific impulse. Useless at sea level.
parts.heritage: Merlin Vacuum, RL10.

parts.name: Vacuum Engine (Large)
parts.description: A high-thrust vacuum engine for heavy payloads. Better efficiency and higher thrust than the small version.
parts.heritage: Based on RL10B-2 and Vinci engines.

parts.name: Pyrotechnic Separation
parts.description: Explosive bolts and springs that push the two stages apart. Proven, cheap, one-shot.
parts.heritage: Standard on every multistage rocket since the 1950s.

parts.name: Hot-Stage Ring
parts.description: The upper stage ignites while still attached. No springs, no pyros, just thrust pushing the stages apart. Reusable, but the interstage must be vented.
parts.heritage: Based on Starship hot-staging and Soviet-era designs.

parts.name: Standard Interstage
parts.description: A light structural cylinder that connects the first and second stages. Jettisoned at separation.
parts.heritage: Every multistage rocket.

parts.name: Heavy Interstage
parts.description: A reinforced interstage for high-mass upper stages or hot-staging. Carries more load but weighs more.
parts.heritage: Based on heavy lift interstage structures.

parts.name: Grid Fins (Small)
parts.description: Titanium lattice fins that steer the vehicle during atmospheric ascent. Deployed after max-Q.
parts.heritage: Falcon 9, Soyuz.

parts.name: Grid Fins (Large)
parts.description: Larger control surfaces for heavier vehicles flying through thicker atmosphere.
parts.heritage: Falcon Heavy, Starship-class vehicles.

parts.name: Pressurant System
parts.description: Helium composite-overwrapped pressure vessels and regulators that keep the tanks pressurised as propellant drains.
parts.heritage: Standard on all liquid propellant rockets.

parts.name: Autogenous Pressurisation
parts.description: Taps hot gas from the engine to pressurise the tanks. Eliminates helium but requires more engine complexity.
parts.heritage: Starship, Raptor engines.

parts.name: Intertank Structure
parts.description: A composite cylinder that connects the fuel and oxidizer tanks and carries structural loads between them.
parts.heritage: SLS core stage intertank, Ariane 5.

parts.name: Heavy Intertank
parts.description: Reinforced intertank for heavy lift vehicles. Carries more axial load and supports larger tanks.
parts.heritage: SLS, Saturn V.

parts.name: RP-1 Kerosene Tank
parts.description: Refined kerosene. Dense, storable, and well understood. The workhorse fuel of the last sixty years.
parts.heritage: Falcon 9, Saturn V first stage, Soyuz.

parts.name: Liquid Methane Tank
parts.description: Liquid methane. Cleaner burning than kerosene, easier to store than hydrogen, and manufacturable on Mars from local CO2 and water.
parts.heritage: Starship, Raptor engines, Blue Origin BE-4.

parts.name: Liquid Hydrogen Tank
parts.description: Liquid hydrogen. The highest specific impulse of any practical chemical fuel, but very low density and it boils off over time.
parts.heritage: SLS core stage, Centaur, Ariane 5 ECA.

parts.name: LOX Tank
parts.description: Liquid oxygen. The standard oxidiser for almost every liquid rocket. Non-toxic, but it boils off over days to weeks.
parts.heritage: Every major launch vehicle.

parts.name: N2O4 Tank
parts.description: Nitrogen tetroxide. Hypergolic with hydrazine, storable at room temperature, and used for decades on deep space probes.
parts.heritage: Cassini, Voyager, most deep space missions.

parts.name: Standard Thrust Structure
parts.description: A truss assembly that distributes engine thrust into the tank walls. Without it, the engines rip free of the tank.
parts.heritage: Every liquid rocket has one.

parts.name: Heavy Thrust Structure
parts.description: Reinforced thrust structure for high-thrust or high-mass first stages.
parts.heritage: SLS, Falcon Heavy centre core.

parts.name: Merlin Cluster (9x)
parts.description: Nine sea-level kerolox engines arranged in an octaweb. High thrust, restartable, and one of the most reliable engine configurations in service.
parts.heritage: Falcon 9 first stage, 2010 to present.

parts.name: RS-25 Cluster (4x)
parts.description: Four hydrogen-oxygen engines adapted from the Space Shuttle main engines. Extremely high specific impulse but requires liquid hydrogen.
parts.heritage: Space Shuttle, SLS.

parts.name: Raptor Cluster (3x)
parts.description: Three full-flow staged combustion methalox engines. High thrust, high efficiency, and designed for reuse.
parts.heritage: Starship.

parts.name: Small Solid Booster
parts.description: A small strap-on solid rocket. Adds thrust at liftoff and is jettisoned a few minutes later.
parts.heritage: Ariane 6, H-IIA.

parts.name: Large Liquid Booster
parts.description: A large strap-on booster with its own liquid engine. More thrust than solid, and can be throttled.
parts.heritage: Falcon Heavy side boosters.

parts.name: Reaction Control System
parts.description: A cluster of small thrusters that orient the spacecraft in vacuum. Required for any attitude change after the main engine shuts down.
parts.heritage: Every spacecraft since the 1960s.
